summary: This page is the rospkg v0.2.0 documentation section on ROS environment variable access. It lists the ROS package-related environment variables (ROS_PACKAGE_PATH, ROS_ROOT, ROS_HOME, ROS_LOG_DIR, ROS_TEST_RESULTS_DIR) and describes the rospkg helper functions that read them, with fallback defaults when overrides are not set. Navigation and site boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Documentation for rospkg's functions and environment variables (ROS_ROOT, ROS_HOME, ROS_LOG_DIR and others) used to locate ROS package paths, logs and test results.
key_facts: The rospkg environment APIs provide access to ROS package-related environment variables, including methods that supply default values when environment variable overrides are not active.
The documented environment variables are ROS_PACKAGE_PATH, ROS_ROOT, ROS_HOME, ROS_LOG_DIR and ROS_TEST_RESULTS_DIR.
get_ros_root(env=None) returns a str and gets the current ROS_ROOT.
get_ros_home(env=None) returns a str giving the location of the .ros directory, also known as ROS_HOME.
For get_ros_home, the ROS_LOG_DIR environment variable has priority; if it is not set, ROS_HOME/log is used, and if ROS_HOME is not set, $HOME/.ros/log is used.
get_log_dir(env=None) returns a str giving the directory for writing log files, using the same priority order as get_ros_home: ROS_LOG_DIR, then ROS_HOME/log, then $HOME/.ros/log.
get_test_results_dir(env=None) returns a str giving the directory for writing test result files.
For get_test_results_dir, if ROS_TEST_RESULTS_DIR is set it is returned; otherwise ROS_HOME/test_results is used, and if ROS_HOME is not set, $HOME/.ros/test_results is used.
on_ros_path(p, env=None) returns a bool indicating whether a filesystem path is on the paths specified in the ROS environment (ROS_ROOT, ROS_PACKAGE_PATH).
Each function that takes an env parameter accepts an override environment dictionary.
